assumptions: Coach acceptance rate of AI-drafted replies and per-log edit data will be captured from day one (events + coach_draft diff).
Athlete consent can be written to allow the athlete to carry their own logs across gyms while coach notes stay with the gym.
Founding gyms are 50-200 adult-member combat gyms in the NYC/NJ area; the founder is not selling to MK.
Cost to serve stays near $7/gym + $1.25/coached member; per-member pricing ($5) or tiered flat ($99/$249/$499) as decided.
No paid acquisition; distribution is founder-led, referral and affiliation-driven.

insights.insight: The platform threat is now a single $7.5B company that already ships AI (Messenger[ai], EGYM Genius) to 40,000 gyms.
insights.evidence: Playlist (Mindbody/ClassPass) merged with EGYM at $7.5B, March 2026; 40k Mindbody businesses, 88k ClassPass venues (TechCrunch).
insights.implication: Any moat that lives inside the owner's dashboard will be bundled away; defensibility must sit with the athlete, the coach, or the sport.

insights.insight: Incumbent retention tooling is attendance-based and reactive.
insights.evidence: Gymdesk 'Absence' trigger fires after N days without attendance; PushPress flags declining check-ins (Gymdesk docs, PushPress).
insights.implication: Signals from what athletes *say* (injury, 'stuck', frustration) arrive weeks before attendance drops; that data stream is unclaimed.

insights.insight: Members stay for people and accountability, not price.
insights.evidence: Retention drivers: friendly staff 31%, community 20%, accountability 17% (Sogolytics n=1,069 via Athletech).
insights.implication: A product that manufactures coach attention is aligned with the true retention lever; a dashboard is not.

insights.insight: Injury is a routine, recurring event in combat sports and drives long absences.
insights.evidence: 81% of BJJ practitioners injured per year, ~34 days lost per injury (PMC n=881); NCAA wrestling 9.28 injuries/1,000 exposures.
insights.implication: An injury/return-to-training record is high-value, longitudinal, and something no gym software holds today.

insights.insight: Amateur matchmaking still runs on paper passbooks and improvised rooms.
insights.evidence: 'Hundreds of documents floating around'; officials work 'with no heat, air, or even a table' (The Glowing Edge). BoutFinder exists for boxing clubs only.
insights.implication: A verified digital record (weight, experience, injury clearance) is a wedge into an exchange nobody owns across striking and grappling.

insights.insight: Exchange-type networks in sport become near-monopolies once adopted.
insights.evidence: Hudl reached ~95% of US HS football because opponent film is only available on-platform; switching means 'going dark' (SGX report).
insights.implication: If gyms/promoters depend on Cornerwork records to match fights or sparring, leaving carries a real competitive cost.

insights.insight: Combat sports distribution is concentrated in affiliations.
insights.evidence: Gracie Barra ~700-1,000 schools, Nova União ~392, Alliance ~305 (BJJEE); WTBA and USA Muaythai list affiliated gyms.
insights.implication: One affiliation head adopting a coaching-note standard is worth hundreds of individual gym sales and hard for a horizontal vendor to displace.

insights.insight: Athletes already self-log without being asked.
insights.evidence: BJJ Notes reports 30k+ users; Grappling AI sells voice-note logging at $3.99/mo; many Amazon BJJ journals.
insights.implication: The athlete-side habit exists; the missing piece is the coach loop and portability, not the logging behaviour.

insights.insight: Coach pay is the operational bottleneck and the incumbents have no concept of it.
insights.evidence: At $8/member coaches earn ~$18/hr; at $10/member with AI drafts ~$35-50/hr (session model). Gym software prices per location and sells to owners only.
insights.implication: A revenue share that pays coaches is counter-positioned: copying it forces incumbents to reprice and rebuild payouts.

insights.insight: Payments turn vertical software into infrastructure.
insights.evidence: Mindbody earned ~$150 subscription + ~$100 payments per customer; fintech lifts revenue/customer 2-5x (a16z).
insights.implication: Moving the coached-tier money (and coach payouts) through Cornerwork raises switching cost and revenue per gym.

insights.insight: SMB SaaS churn is high and front-loaded.
insights.evidence: 3-5% monthly churn for ACV <$10k; 70% of churn in the first 90 days (Optifai, 939 companies).
insights.implication: Moats must show value inside 90 days; slow-compounding moats need a fast-value wrapper.

insights.insight: Coach-reviewed corrections are a labeled dataset no one else can collect.
insights.evidence: Every coach edit of an AI draft is a (context, draft, correction) triple in the sport's own language; incumbents have no coach in the loop.
insights.implication: A sport-specific coaching model becomes measurably better than a generic LLM with scale; the gap widens with every log.

insights.insight: Integration access is controlled by the incumbent.
insights.evidence: Mindbody API is gated (manual approval, per-site activation, metered); Gymdesk exposes only Zapier triggers.
insights.implication: Any moat that depends on incumbent APIs is revocable; the product must work with CSV and opt-in alone.

insights.insight: Consent and safety handling are regulatory surface area that small competitors skip.
insights.evidence: TCPA statutory damages $500-1,500 per unwanted text; concussion/injury data adjacent to health law; confidential-concern routing.
insights.implication: Documented consent, injury and concussion handling can become a standard that sanctioning bodies or insurers reference.

recommended_portfolio.strategy_title: Coach-correction corpus: the sport's own coaching model
recommended_portfolio.rationale: Starts on day one at near-zero cost, compounds with every reply, and is the one asset a $7.5B platform cannot buy or bundle because it has no coach in the loop.
Structurally opposed to the incumbents' gym-owns-member model; turns every gym change into distribution and gives athletes a reason to keep the product independent of any gym.

recommended_portfolio.strategy_title: Affiliation standard: one network head adopts the coaching-note format
recommended_portfolio.rationale: Only founder-specific distribution lever that reaches hundreds of gyms without paid acquisition, and it feeds the corpus and passport with volume.

kill_criteria.strategy_title: Coach-correction corpus: the sport's own coaching model
criteria: Draft acceptance rate below 25% at month 3 with no upward trend across two consecutive months
Fewer than 1,500 labeled corrections by month 6 across all gyms
Blind eval shows no measurable gain over the base model at 5k corrections
Fewer than 30% of coached athletes open their progress page in any month by month 4
Zero athletes carry the passport to a new gym by month 9
Two of three founding owners refuse portability terms after seeing the consent split

kill_criteria.strategy_title: Affiliation standard: one network head adopts the coaching-note format
criteria: No affiliation head agrees to a pilot by month 6 after 5+ conversations
Affiliate schools onboard at a CAC above $400 or churn above 5%/month
HQ demands cash terms that push gym-level margin below 50%
